## What it is

A machine-learning system that classifies amateur-radio modes directly from RF
(IQ) data. The long-term aim is a pipeline that can look at a stretch of
spectrum, find the signals in it, identify each mode, and decode what it can:
**capture → detect → identify → decode → annotate**.

The current version has two parts:

- a **harvester** that records real off-air IQ from public KiwiSDRs and labels
  it with the decoders themselves (jt9 for FT8 and FT4, Baudot, Morse and PSK
  decoders for the keyed modes, Whisper and a human vote for voice), and
- a **narrowband IQ classifier**, a small CNN trained on those recordings and
  judged on receivers it never saw.

## Why I built it

It grew out of watching FT8 decode stations I couldn't even hear, and wondering
how much of the "which mode is this?" work could be done automatically. The
long-term goal is a live assistant that can scan a band, tell you what's on it
and decode what it finds, eventually as an overlay for an SDR such as a
FlexRadio.

## Current status & goals

- **The synthetic approach failed.** The first version, trained on validated
  synthetic generators and measured on a synthetic benchmark, scored 99% and
  fell over on the first real receiver. That result is withdrawn; the
  [post](../blog-posts/2026-10-14-the-signals-were-real-this-time/2026-10-14-the-signals-were-real-this-time.qmd)
  explains why.
- **Real data instead.** Three weeks of harvesting from 15 public receivers
  gave 4,241 recordings, about 9 GB of IQ, and roughly 28,000 decoder-verified
  labels across FT8, FT4, RTTY and CW, plus voted voice clips. A label exists
  only where a decoder actually read the signal; skimmer spots confirm labels
  but never create them.
- **First honest result.** Trained on ten receivers and tested on three it
  never saw: balanced accuracy 0.97. FT8 and CW 0.99, RTTY 0.97, noise 1.00,
  FT4 0.88. The learning curve is flat from a quarter of the data upwards, and
  the model's features separate by mode rather than by receiver.
- **Known limits.** Strong signals only (every label is at least 6 dB over the
  floor), voice thin, FT4 confused with RTTY, no PSK31 or multi-tone modes yet,
  three European KiwiSDRs as judges.
- **Goals:** a confidence threshold with an "unsure" output, a weak-signal test
  by mixing recorded noise into decoded signals, more voice votes, release of
  the dataset as IQ and mode labels, and then the live identify-and-decode
  interface.

## Key links

- [WSJT-X](https://wsjtx.github.io/wsjtx/index.html), whose jt9 labels the FT8
  and FT4 recordings
- [KiwiSDR public receivers](http://rx.linkfanel.net/), the source of the
  off-air recordings
- [Reverse Beacon Network](https://www.reversebeacon.net/), used to confirm CW
  and RTTY labels by callsign
- [fldigi](https://sourceforge.net/projects/fldigi/), the reference decoder used
  to validate the keyed-mode decoders
